EventItemActionText:
The Board of Zoning Appeals met for a regular meeting in the Vienna Town Hall at 127 Center St S, Vienna, Virginia, on Wednesday, September 18, 2024. Chairman Mr. Dhanjal called the meeting to order at 7:30 pm. 
Roll Call: Mr. Lowther, Mr. Petersen, Mr. Rettinger, Mr. Creed, Mr. Gadell, Mr. Nash, and Mr. Dhanjal were present. 

Staff present: David Levy, Director of Planning and Zoning, Andrea West Zoning Administrator, Kelly O’Brien, Deputy Director of Planning and Zoning and Board Clerk Yaska Camacho Castillo. 

Chairman Dhanjal opened the Public Meeting at 7:35 PM noting that Agenda Items 1 and 2 will be discussed in reverse order.

Andrea West, Zoning Administrator, provided the board with a PowerPoint presentation that included information about the site location, future land use & zoning, zoning regulations code section 18-324, pictures of the front and side view as well a picture of the existing screening, the family day home entry, the outdoor play area, the family day home interior, and the parking analysis.

In summary, the proposed conditional use permit to expand the existing family day home to up to 12 children does align with the comprehensive plan which has a note about family day homes and daycares being part of the economy. Ms. West noted that the zoning ordinance requires adequate parking for a family day home. 
Applicants - Hesham Ibrahim and Youssef Ibrahim were sworn in to provide testimony. Youssef Ibrahim provided the board with his statement at 7:45 p.m. 

Mr. Petersen stated as clarification that the Board of Zoning Appeals does have the authority to set limits.  Should the applicant wish to limit the number of children in the application to fewer than twelve, they can do so. 
Mr. Petersen requested clarification of the written application statement that “the operator of the facility will live mostly in the facility”. The applicant indicated that the operator may spend weekends at the 305 Jade Ct. location, but weekdays will be spent at the 304 Jade Ct. location. 

Additional comments and questions from the Board included the following:
Mr. Rettinger commended the applicants for an admirable service to the community and asked the applicants if they had thought about opening a commercial space. Mr. Youssel Ibrahim stated that the family has considered moving the business to a commercial site. Due to the rapid movement of the leasing market, it has been difficult to find an appropriate location.

The applicant reports that the two daycare facilities coordinate pickup/drop-off. An attendance sheet with assigned pickup/drop-off is utilized. The driveway is kept open to clients. 

The two businesses are stated to be separate yet said to overlap. By way of explanation, the applicant indicated that the businesses are separate in that they have different schedules of operation.

The board voiced their concerns about the proximity of the two daycares being side by side and the parking in the small size cul-de-sac (nine homes).

Chairman Dhanjal opened the floor for comment from the public.

Lindsey Johnston, 302 Jade Ct., NW was sworn in to speak.

Ms. Johnston testified against the request for the conditional use permit stating that when she first moved in, she wasn’t aware of the daycares in the cul-de-sac. She is concerned about the traffic flow and noted that every night there are very bright lights along their property facing her house, glaring at her son’s window.  

In response to a question from the Board, the speaker indicated that the lights were on throughout the evening and even occasionally all night.  It was noted that the Town Code states that outdoor lighting is to be shielded so as not to project onto a neighbor’s property.  The property in question is fairly denuded from vegetation. Other daycare facilities have been required to provide vegetation to buffer between properties. This facility should also be required to install buffering.

Suki Singh, 307 Jade Ct. NW - was sworn in to speak. 

Mr. Singh was not in favor of the conditional use permit. He voiced his concern about the traffic flow due to the surrounding schools (James Madison High School, Louise Archer, Kinder Care, Happy Hour, and Green Hedges) in the area. He feels that the request to increase the enrollment to 12 children would be detrimental to the neighbors and the kids who live or come to play in the cul-de-sac.

Harbans Singh, 301 Jade Ct. NW - was sworn in to speak. 

Mr. Singh stated he did not support the request to increase the enrollment to twelve (12) children due to the heavy traffic and quality of life. 
Harpreet Multani, 300 Jade Ct. NW- was sworn in to speak.

Ms. Multani testified against the request stating that when the family first started their daycare it was only for twelve (12) children and over time the applicants rented the property across the street to start another daycare overall, increasing the number of children from twelve (12) to sixteen (16). The speaker also mentioned that with all the vehicles coming in and out of the neighborhood the children are not allowed to play safely or use the basketball hoop due to the traffic.  She also expressed her concern with how the neighborhood felt more like a commercial site area with two daycares side by side and the traffic flow. 

Lyn Beer, 302 Lewis St NW – was sworn in to speak. 

Ms. Beer stated that she lives behind the property under consideration.  She sees the children are supervised while playing and they seem very happy.  It seems to be a lovely place for children. She said that there is little traffic around Jade Ct and Knoll in comparison to what goes on around the rest of the neighborhood. Ms. Beer understands the parents want their children to be able to play outside but noted that the street is not intended for that purpose. The streets are designed for cars, not for bicycles. Kids are not supposed to play in the street; they are supposed to play in their yards, on the sidewalk, a playground, or someplace safe.  

Bernard Rothschild, 8904 Mears St., Fairfax, VA – was sworn to speak. 

Mr. Rothschild was in favor of the application. He stated that when he drops off his son in the morning the traffic in the area is not from Jade Ct. As a parent, he understands safety issues, but from his experience, the drop-off and pickup, are 2-3 minutes. He feels that the applicants and neighbors should have sat down and come up with an agreement on how many additional children would be acceptable as he believes this is a solvable issue. No one is questioning the applicants' ability to take care of the children, but the neighbors don’t want more kids because of the additional traffic it may cause. Although he doesn’t that’s entirely the problem.  He believes they just don’t want another daycare in the neighborhood. He said there should be love for what they do, not animosity for all the possible outcomes. 

Mr. Rothschild noted that the applicants haven’t had any violations. It would be a shame that they might not have the opportunity to expand.  There’s a lot of negative energy and he thinks this should be hashed out so this family can have the ability to serve more children.  He trusts Youssef and his father with my kids.  If they cannot expand, he doesn’t know what he will do as childcare is expensive. The cost of Kinder Care for two children is $5,000/month. It would be unfair if the daycare wasn’t allowed to expand.  They have indicated that they would accept a smaller expansion, and he thinks that is fair. 

Elizabeth DiFrancisco, 434 Knoll St., NW – was sworn in to speak.

Ms. DiFranciso was against the application. She said that families from all over the neighborhood bring their children to Jade Ct. so they can ride their bikes safely referencing Ms. Beer’s testimony. She stated that her children (in their late 20’s) learned how to play baseball, how to ride their bikes, to play basketball – all on Jade Ct.  There needs to be somewhere safe to play.  They can’t play at Louise Archer after school because it’s under renovation.  The kids in the neighborhood want Jade Ct. to be the sanctuary it has been for the past 25 years and on into perpetuity.  

Furthermore, Ms. DiFrancisco commented about the traffic staggering, saying that while she was walking yesterday at 5:00 PM she saw five cars enter Jade Ct. and all vehicles stopped at 304 Jade Ct. After seven minutes those cars were still there, so there wasn’t staggering of pickup. Having a timesheet is great, but the truth is, that all parents come as soon as work is over, and they are all arriving at the same time. Additionally, the speaker encouraged the board to further delve into which family lives because the conditional use permit stipulates full-time residents, and the neighbors aren’t witnessing full-time residents at 305 Jade Ct. The applicants stated under oath that they don’t always live there on the weekend which indicated no full-time residents of the address.

Penny Ellen Osak, 221 Nutley St., NW – was sworn in to speak. 

Ms. Osak voiced her concerns about traffic and safety.  She noted that she does not live on Jade Ct. but she walks in the area every day. Jade Ct and Knoll St have heavy traffic from 3:30 PM-4:00 PM. The neighbors supported a daycare at 305 Jade Ct.  The applicants then leased a second home and were allowed four children at 304 Jade Ct by right.  The applicants then asked the neighbors for support to expand from 4 children to 12 making the expansion to a total of 24 children between both locations and the neighbors said no, enough is enough. 

Additionally, Ms. Osak noted that Jade Ct is a small cul-de-sac where the children have liked to come to play for the past 25 years. It is unfair to tell the children that they can no longer play in the cul-de-sac because of the two-family daycares, a total of 24 children coming and going every day. She understands that the family home business is a need in the Town, but they need to ensure that they understand the neighbors' concerns and how their quality of life will be impacted.  

Sheri Dart, 331 Lewis St. NW was sworn in to speak. 

Ms. Dart stated that she has been an active walker for a long time.  She usually uses Jade Ct., and has not noticed any problems with traffic in the Ct. There are lots of pickups from Louise Archer School on Knoll St and Lewis St. For this reason, she likes to walk along Knoll and Jade because there’s not so much traffic. 

Ms. Dart commented about other locations where children can play besides the cul-de-sac. Green Hedges has been around for over 80 years. They’ve always allowed kids to play there on the weekends. Sara Walker Mercer Park is also a nice play area. 

Chairman Dhanjal recognized the applicant to respond to issues presented by the speakers. Mr. Yusuf Ibrahim addressed the light [comment mentioned by one speaker] which has been on the property for a long time.  It is unrelated to the daycare and is used to provide light on the Court after dark. 

The issue of stacked cars [mentioned by another speaker] was due to the rainy/stormy weather yesterday.  Rather than parents coming into the facility, they brought the children out to the cars.

Chairman Dhanjal asked if there were any additional comments to which Mr. Creed stated that a few written comments were received this afternoon, and he wants to ensure those comments are included in the record tonight.  Mr. Dhanjal reminded all that last-minute written comments have been uploaded to Granicus.  With no additional public comment, Chairman Dhanjal called for a motion to close the public hearing at 8:45 PM.

Motion: Mr. Nash
Second: Mr. Lowther
The motion carried unanimously in a roll call vote.

At this time Chairman Dhanjal read into the record the charge of the Board of Zoning Appeals.          

The closed portion of the discussion opened with a motion on the Item.

Mr. Petersen made a motion to approve the request for a conditional use permit (CUP) per Section 18-304 of the Vienna Town Code for a Family Day Home to care for up to seven (7) children at 304 Jade Court NW, in the 12.5 zoning district for a term of three years.

Motion: Mr. Peterson
Second: Mr. Nash

The board’s discussion included the following points:
• The proposed expansion will have a positive impact on the Town of Vienna.  It brings expansion of a needed service; it would not adversely affect the health or safety of people residing or walking in the neighborhood; it won’t be detrimental to the public welfare or injurious to property or improvements in the neighborhood. 
•  It is in accordance with the Comprehensive Plan of the Town of Vienna.  It certainly meets the specific standards that are outlined in Article 3, Chapter 18-324.  
• The applicant also stated they would only have seven children in care, so that is why the identified limit.  Further, a three-year limit is set due to concerns raised and stated opposition by some individuals living on Jade Ct. This will provide the opportunity for all involved to fairly assess the impact of these additional seven children.

Mr. Petersen stated that the issues raised about lighting at night can be addressed separately.  Traffic on Knoll St. can be raised separately (related to the three schools mentioned earlier) with the Town of Vienna. The applicants have met the burden of showing that this would contribute to the welfare of Vienna and would not adversely affect the neighborhood. Mr. Peterson noted that he purposely did not bring up landscaping because he did not want that to be part of his motion. 

Chairman Dhanjal called for comment from the Board.  Comments are summarized as follows:

•  There are possible safety issues with adding more children to this facility; Uncertain that this body is appropriate to judge whether additional children will be injurious to property.
• Cars don’t typically travel 50 MPH on a cul-de-sac; don’t believe there is a safety issue; could be a case of “not in my backyard”; Believe benefit outweighs inconvenience; Urge give and take from all parties involved.
• Uncertain why Planning Commission and Town Council allowed this Conditional Use Permit for a family daycare even though it is important and needed in the community; Neither body appears to have considered the impact of two daycare facilities in one cul-de-sac. The meeting minutes from the Planning Commission included a 6-0 vote to recommend that the Board of Zoning Appeals not approve the CUP; Minutes also included that the expansion of this childcare service would be detrimental to the neighborhood; and urged the Board to pay attention to this recommendation. 
• Business appears to be a commercial enterprise; recommend moving to a rented commercial space.
• Must consider that the approval of this CUP would change the nature of the neighborhood; Two of nine residential housing businesses are a large percentage for a residential neighborhood.
• The Applicant was congratulated on two very successful businesses. These businesses have provided a much-needed service to the community and have helped the Town grow, but the neighbors have reached a saturation point.
• Have an option to make a motion without prejudice as a way to allow the applicant room for reapplication if a compromise is reached with neighbors.
• Caution against setting a bad precedent that the application can be denied if neighbors oppose (despite the value and quality of service provided).
• Must highlight the saturation of this type of business in a small neighborhood.

With no additional comments from the Board, Chairman Dhanjal called for a motion to close the debate.

Motion: Mr. Lowther
Second: Mr. Rettinger
The motion carried unanimously.

Chairman Dhanjal called for a vote on the motion on the floor.
Aye: Mr. Petersen, Mr. Nash
Nay: Mr. Rettinger, Mr. Gadell, Mr. Creed, Mr. Lowther, Mr. Dhanjal
Motion failed in a 5-2 vote.

Mr. Lowther made a motion to deny the request for a conditional use permit (CUP) per Section 18-304 of the Vienna Town Code for a Family Day Home to care for up to twelve (12) children at 304 Jade Court NW, in the 12.5 zoning district without prejudice to a new application as allowed.

Motion: Mr. Lowther
Second: Mr. Gadell

The board questioned the need for a second motion if the motion to approve a daycare for up to seven (7) children was denied. Mr. Dhanjal explained that from his point of view, the application is requesting to care for up to twelve (12) children therefore a motion addressing that request is needed. 

David Levy, Director, Planning and Zoning was sworn in to clarify the motion.  He confirmed that it is necessary to vote on the application for twelve children.  Andrea West, Zoning Administrator confirmed that the “without prejudice” need not be added to the motion as there is no limit to the number of times an applicant can apply for a CUP.  Chairman Dhanjal reminded the Board of the appeal process, as well.

Mr. Lowther restated his motion as follows:

Motion to deny the request for a conditional use permit (CUP) per Section 18-304 of the Vienna Town Code for a Family Day Home to care for up to twelve (12) children at 304 Jade Court NW, in the 12.5 zoning district.

Motion: Mr. Lowther
Second: Mr. Gadell

Mr. Petersen indicated for the record that he planned to vote in favor of the motion because the language included twelve (12) children, which he deemed to be too many.

The motion on the floor passed unanimously through a roll call vote.

Chairman Dhanjal reiterated that the applicant is currently operating a very successful business, and they have become a victim of their success.
EventItemTitle: Request approval by the Board of Zoning Appeals for a conditional use permit per Section 18-304 of the Vienna Town Code for a Family Day Home to care for up to twelve (12) children at 304 Jade Court NW, in the 12.5 zoning district. Application filed by Hesham Ibrahim.

Andrea West, Zoning Administrator – 127 Center St South Vienna, VA was sworn in to provide background on agenda item #2. She stated that the applicant submitted a written request earlier today to defer the application. The Town had no additional information to present.

Applicant - Sara Mariska, Odin, Feldman & Pittleman, 1775 Lily Avenue, Ste. 400, Reston, VA representing the Vienna Development Association, LLC., was sworn in to speak. Ms. Mariska stated that she has been working collaboratively with staff to resolve the appeal filed in the hope that the client will be able to withdraw. She is working on filing a site plan to address the stated violations.  The plan must be filed within the next 30 days, so she, on behalf of the client, is requesting a deferral of the public hearing until November 20, 2024.  

Chairman Dhanjal opened the floor for discussion from the Board. Mr. Petersen asked if the board deferred the application, would it have any effect on the timetable for the imposition of any sanctions or relief from what the town has filed?  Ms. West clarified that once an appeal is filed that action “stays” any further enforcement action from the Town. If no communication was received from the applicant the town could have moved forward with civil penalties, and possibly court action. 

With no further comments, Chairman Dhanjal called for a motion to close the Public Hearing. 

Mr. Petersen made a motion to accept the request for a deferment to a public hearing until November 20, 2024.

Motion: Mr. Peterson
Second: Mr. Creed.  
Motion carried unanimously.

About the Board of Zoning Appeals

About the Board of Zoning Appeals:

The Board of Zoning Appeals is a quasi-judicial board comprised of seven members – all of whom are residents of the Town of Vienna, VA.  The Board serves as an arm of the Fairfax County Circuit Court, as all members are appointed to the Board by the Court after receipt of recommendation from the Vienna Mayor and Town Council. 

The Board is empowered by the Code of Virginia to:

•Hear and decide appeals from any order, requirement, decision or determination of the Zoning Administrator.
•Grant variances from the Zoning Ordinance – as defined in Section 15.2201 of the Code of Virginia – as will not be contrary to the public interest, when, owing to special conditions, a literal enforcement of the provisions will unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property to a degree that is not shared generally by other properties within the same zone or district, and its authorization will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent properties or change the character of the neighborhood
•Hear and decide applications for interpretation of the Zoning District Map when there is any uncertainty as to the location of the boundary line.
•Grant Conditional Use Permits in accordance with the provisions of Section 18-209 – 216 of the Vienna Town Code.

The Board of Zoning Appeals does not have the power to change the Zoning Ordinance or the rezone property.  Those powers rest with the Mayor and Town Council.  Please be advised, the Board decides each application on its own merit – there are no precedents.

The Board will first consider each application during the Public Hearing portion of the meeting.  As part of the Virginia Court System, the Board of Zoning Appeals takes sworn testimony and each participant will be sworn in prior to offering comments.  During the public hearing each agenda shall be closed a decision will be rendered. 

The grant of a Conditional Use Permit, Variance, or appeal from a decision by the Town’s Zoning Administrator requires an affirmative vote of no less than a majority of membership, of the Board. The Board consists of 7 members and a majority consists 4 members.  If the applicant is unable to stay for the Board’s decision portion, the applicant may learn the Board’s decision by contacting staff.  

The second portion of the meeting – the Regular Meeting – is for approval of meeting minutes and new business and will convene after the Public Hearing has been closed.  

If any party is not satisfied with the decision of the Board, an appeal may be filed with the Circuit Court of Fairfax County within 30 days after the issuance of the Board’s decision on the matter.
